title_as_printed: Mole fraction of CO2 in water at given pressures and temperatures

footnotes_as_printed.a: H, Lw, and V are the solid hydrate, liquid water, and vapor, respectively.

pressure_note: Header 'Pressure (bar)'; text: constant experimental pressure maintained by supplying CO2; not stated whether total or CO2 partial. In H-Lw rows (above three-phase line) the gas was displaced by water, so the pressure is that of the liquid-hydrate system. Experiments 'conducted at the three-phase equilibrium and in the hydrate formation region'.
volume_basis_evidence: quantity is a mole fraction, no per-volume definition

composition.other_species: pure CO2 in distilled deionized water

extra_unmapped: Phases present (H solid hydrate, Lw liquid water, V vapour)
notes: xeq derived by the authors' analytic flash method from gas volume released in a gasometer plus Henry-law correction at room T (eq 2, uses literature CO2 solubility at room conditions); authors give relative error 3-5 percent of the calculated solubility. Treated as the measured result. Rows 15-20 (Lw-V, no hydrate) are labelled 'below the three-phase equilibrium' in the text. Rows with T < 273.15 K: none.
